and drew near to the wall of Damietta,
and began to wage war from the water.
Now the people of Damietta, because al-Kamil and his forces were nearby,
and all their supplies were coming in to them from the land,
cared nothing about the Franks.
Then God willed, and news of the death of al-Adil in Damascus reached his son al-Kamil;
and [it was reported] that the Emir Ibn al-Mashtub and the rest of the Kurdish Hakkari emirs wished to set up al-Malik al-Fa'iz, the brother of al-Kamil,
as king in Egypt.
And on account of this, al-Kamil took his forces and set out for Egypt,
and abandoned Damietta.
Then the Franks took courage and came out onto the dry land,
and captured the rest of the baggage that had been left behind in the camp of the Arabs.
And they encamped against Damietta,
and began to wage war against it from the sea and from the land.
Now the people of Damietta, because they were waiting for the help that was to come to them from the Arabs,
held out greatly in the battle.
And the Franks remained for about nine months while waging war against it.
And when the Arabs inside despaired of help,
because al-Kamil was not able to come out of Egypt,
for he was afraid of treachery,
they therefore surrendered to the Franks,
and delivered the city up to them in peace.
And when the Franks took Damietta,
they proclaimed that whoever of the Arabs wished to leave with his provisions might leave,
and whoever [wished] to remain might remain.
And many did not leave.
Now al-Kamil, when he saw the boldness of the Franks, feared {OCR} them greatly;
and he sent and destroyed the walls of Jerusalem,
so that it might not be a stronghold for the Franks when they should take it.
And at this time, when he was hard-pressed,
Rupen the Frank, the lord of Antioch, by Prince [Bohemond] the One-eyed, his uncle, the lord of Tripoli,
because King Leo had neglected him on account of the fact that he was prepared to repay him evil instead of good,
abandoned Antioch,
and came to Henri [John],
the king of the Franks, at Damietta,
and stayed with him until he died. The legate of the Pope of Rome
